title: SecureRAG: End-to-End Secure Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Separates retrieval into secure search and secure document fetching, using fully homomorphic encryption for encrypted vector search and attribute-based encryption for fine-grained document access. The system supports dynamic database updates and adaptive access policies.

admission.reason: Its secure-search and attribute-based document-fetching capabilities fit TF9, but for this reading round they are substantially redundant with the admitted VERIFIED paper 2508.01084, which also constrains retrieval to authorized entities and adds formal security arguments. The candidate is UNCHECKED and the abstract does not add the permission-aware replenishment loop required by gap-4.

title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation
abstract: Introduces a retrieval evaluator that estimates the quality of retrieved evidence and triggers different corrective actions when evidence is weak. The framework can extend retrieval with web search and decomposes and recomposes retrieved information before generation.

admission.reason: Topic words match iterative retrieval, but the abstract describes a coarse retrieval-quality evaluator that selects corrective actions such as web search. It does not represent the exact missing evidence, preserve temporal/version or authorization constraints, or provide a bounded stopping criterion. The current corpus needs evidence-gap and stopping mechanisms beyond generic weak-retrieval correction.

title: TempQA: An LLM-based framework for temporal knowledge graph question answering
abstract: Presents a zero-shot temporal knowledge-graph QA framework that converts temporal graph facts into text, retrieves semantically relevant temporal facts, and uses an LLM to reason over them.

admission.reason: The paper performs temporal knowledge-graph QA by retrieving semantically relevant temporal facts, but the abstract does not show temporal-intent ranking over changing document collections, version identity, freshness control, or iterative evidence-gap acquisition. Its temporal vocabulary therefore does not materially close TF5 or the version-aware gap-2.

title: Best of Both Worlds: Towards Improving Temporal Knowledge Base Question Answering via Targeted Fact Extraction
abstract: Addresses temporal question answering when a knowledge base lacks the facts required to answer a query. It uses targeted temporal fact extraction to supplement the knowledge base when retrieval alone cannot supply the needed evidence.

admission.reason: The targeted temporal fact-extraction mechanism is relevant to missing knowledge, but the abstract primarily supplements an incomplete temporal knowledge base rather than controlling bounded document retrieval. It does not retain version lineage, authorization, explicit sufficiency decisions, or stopping state, and MRAG plus VersionRAG are materially closer to the open temporal/version retrieval gaps.

title: A Taxonomy of Time in Databases
abstract: Develops a taxonomy for representing time in database systems and distinguishes multiple temporal dimensions needed to describe changing information. This work is foundational for separating when facts are valid from when they are stored or recorded.

admission.reason: The temporal-database taxonomy is foundationally relevant, but its contribution for this round is substantially redundant with the admitted 1994 consensus glossary, which more directly standardizes valid-time and transaction-time terminology. Reading both is not justified by the current open gaps, especially because this record is also UNCHECKED.

title: Securing Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Taxonomy of Attacks, Defenses, and Future Directions
abstract: Surveys security risks across the RAG knowledge-access pipeline, organizing attacks and defenses by stages and trust boundaries. It covers retrieval-time manipulation and information-exfiltration risks and observes that existing defenses remain fragmented.

admission.reason: The paper surveys RAG attack and defense categories and observes fragmented security defenses, but the abstract does not contribute an authorization-aware retrieval mechanism, evidence-replenishment controller, or permission-constrained stopping behavior. Security vocabulary alone is out of scope for the targeted controller questions.

title: Secure Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Preventing Data Leakage with Provenance and Policy Enforcement
abstract: Presents a RAG governance architecture combining identity-aware filtering, attribute-based access control, policy enforcement, provenance tracking, and auditable refusal behavior. Its evaluation considers leakage, entitlement violations, provenance fidelity, and refusal correctness.

admission.reason: The architecture combines identity-aware filtering, ABAC, provenance, and refusal behavior, but the abstract does not show the bounded permission-aware replenishment loop required by gap-4 or the temporal/version/sufficiency integration required by gap-8. Its access-control evidence is also substantially overlapped by the admitted PPPARITL, HONEYBEE, and VERIFIED 2508.01084 candidates, while this identity is UNCHECKED.

title: Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models through Question Complexity
abstract: Introduces a classifier that estimates question complexity and dynamically routes queries among no-retrieval, single-step retrieval, and iterative retrieval strategies, targeting a better effectiveness-efficiency tradeoff.

admission.reason: Adaptive-RAG dynamically routes questions among no retrieval, one retrieval, and iterative retrieval based on predicted question complexity, but the decision is made from the question before evidence acquisition. It therefore does not address the central open problem of reassessing structured evidence sufficiency after each retrieval step or making a calibrated evidence-driven stopping decision.
